title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: SYSK Live: The DB Cooper Heist
summary: Live recording at the Neptune Theatre in Seattle (2017) of the Stuff You Should Know true crime playlist episode on the unsolved 1971 D.B. Cooper hijacking. The hosts walk through the Northwest Orient Flight 305 hijacking from Portland to Seattle on Thanksgiving 1971: the ticket purchase, the bomb note, the ransom of $200,000 and four parachutes, the circling over SeaTac, the release of passengers and crew (flight attendant Tina Mucklow returning to the plane), and Cooper's jump over the Cascades around 8:12 pm. They cover the failed manhunt, the FBI's investigation, the 1980 discovery of ransom money near the Columbia River, the 2008 parachute find in Amboy, Washington, and the many suspects, including Richard McCoy, Dwayne Weber, Kenny Christiansen, and L.D. Cooper. They also cover the Pursuit of D.B. Cooper film, the D.B. Cooper Days festival in Ariel, and the Boeing 727 aft stair safety paddle nicknamed the "Cooper vane." Much of the episode is comedic banter between the hosts and audience.
rerun_of: SYSK Live: The DB Cooper Heist

segments.title: Episode teaser and playlist intro
segments.summary: Josh introduces the true crime playlist episode, recorded live in Seattle in 2017, on the unsolved D.B. Cooper hijacking, and notes the FBI closed its active investigation in 2016.

segments.title: Opening banter at the Neptune Theatre
segments.summary: The hosts joke about sitting down to pee and other off-color banter before restarting the podcast on stage in Seattle.

segments.title: Cooper buys a ticket for Flight 305
segments.summary: Hosts describe a man at Portland airport in November 1971 asking about the Boeing 727 on Flight 305 to Seattle, buying a one-way ticket for twenty dollars, and writing the name Dan Cooper on the voucher.

segments.title: The crew and passengers
segments.summary: The crew of five is introduced (Captain William Scott, co-pilot Robert Rachek, and flight attendants Alice Hancock, Tina Mucklow and Florence Schaffner). Cooper boards with about 37 other passengers, is described in a russet suit and clip-on tie, and orders bourbon and 7-Up.

segments.title: Hijacking context and the bomb note
segments.summary: The hosts explain the wave of 1968-1971 skyjackings and FBI air marshal policy. Cooper hands flight attendant Florence Schaffner a note, then shows her a bag with what appears to be a bomb, and dictates demands: $200,000 in cash, four parachutes, and a refueling truck.

segments.title: Negotiations with SeaTac and the ransom
segments.summary: The crew radios SeaTac, Seattle police refer the matter to the FBI, and the plane circles for about an hour while the money and parachutes are arranged. Passengers are told of mechanical problems.

segments.title: Cooper and Tina Mucklow talk; Tacoma sighting
segments.summary: Cooper sits with flight attendant Tina Mucklow, discussing her home state and nearby Air Force base; he recognizes Tacoma from the air. Mucklow asks if he has a grudge against the airline.

segments.title: Raising the ransom money
segments.summary: Northwest Orient president Donald Nyrop approves payment. The money comes from a First Bank branch in Seattle, with the serial numbers of the twenty-dollar bills recorded beforehand.

segments.title: Parachutes from Seattle Sky Sports
segments.summary: Earl Cossey of Seattle Sky Sports in Issaquah supplies the parachutes, including a military chute, two reserve chutes and a dummy chute. Cooper takes the group to the SeaTac runway and asks for the shades to be lowered, citing sniper fears.

segments.title: Landing and release of passengers
segments.summary: Tina Mucklow goes out to fetch the money and parachutes and returns to the plane. Passengers and two flight attendants are released, and the hosts recount the FAA psychiatrist's profile of the hijacker, which the hosts mock.

segments.title: Banter on the psychiatrist profile
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the FAA psychiatrist's description and about the crew possibly escaping by rope ladder.

segments.title: Refueling and flight plan demands
segments.summary: During refueling Cooper orders food for the crew and offers money to Mucklow. He asks for a flight to Mexico City, is told the plane needs refueling in Reno, and sets flight instructions: altitude below 10,000 feet, flaps at 15 degrees, speed under 200 knots.

segments.title: The jump and the aft staircase
segments.summary: Cooper fashions a handle for the money bag from the pink parachute, then goes to the rear with Mucklow to lower the aft staircase. He sends her back to the cockpit. At 8:12 pm the crew feels a jolt and realizes he has jumped.

segments.title: Manhunt and search
segments.summary: Fighter jets and a helicopter fail to track the plane. Searchers focus on the Lewis River area near Ariel, Washington. A local millionaire rents a submarine to search Lake Merwin, and the CIA scrambles an SR-71 Blackbird.

segments.title: Name mix-up leads to D.B. Cooper
segments.summary: An FBI press conference and a reporter's wire story turn Dan Cooper into D.B. Cooper. The FBI keeps the name, using it to screen hot leads. A 1950s Belgian comic about a Dan Cooper is also noted.

segments.title: Ralph Himmelsbach and the death theory
segments.summary: Agent Ralph Himmelsbach, who became the best-known agent on the case, self-published a book in 1986 and believed Cooper died in the jump.

segments.title: Survival odds and the parachute question
segments.summary: The hosts describe the cold, wind and terrain over the Cascades, the clothing Cooper wore, and the poor choice of military and dummy chutes. They also discuss the FBI's 727 sled test that ruled out jet exhaust.

segments.title: Evidence left behind and the Oregon placard
segments.summary: Cooper's clip-on tie, eight cigarette butts (since lost), a hair on the headrest, and a fingerprint on a SkyMall magazine were left behind. In 1978 hunters found a plastic aft-stair instruction placard in Oregon.

segments.title: Pursuit of D.B. Cooper film
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the 1981 film Pursuit of D.B. Cooper, starring Treat Williams and Robert Duvall, and mock its opening.

segments.title: 1980 ransom money on Tena Bar
segments.summary: In 1980 eight-year-old Brian Ingram finds stacks of the ransom twenty-dollar bills on Tena Bar (Columbia River island) while digging a fire pit. The FBI identifies the serial numbers, and a hydrologist explains the money likely traveled by river flooding.

segments.title: 2008 Amboy parachute find
segments.summary: In 2008 children in Amboy, Washington, find a parachute in the woods. Earl Cossey identifies it as nylon, not Cooper's silk chute. It belonged to pilot Floyd Walling, who bailed out in 1945.

segments.title: Confessions and sketch
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the many false confessions and the only composite sketch, from flight attendant Tina Mucklow, which resembles Don Draper-style looks.

segments.title: Profiling Cooper: military or airline insider
segments.summary: Hosts discuss theories that Cooper was ex-military or an airline employee, based on the chute choice and his knowledge of the plane's aft staircase, which was then not widely known.

segments.title: Richard McCoy suspect
segments.summary: Richard McCoy, a Green Beret who hijacked a 727 in February 1972 and got $500,000, is discussed as a suspect. He was later killed after escaping prison, and his family said he was home at Thanksgiving 1971.

segments.title: Dwayne Weber deathbed confession
segments.summary: Career criminal Dwayne Weber reportedly confessed to his wife Joe on his deathbed. She later decided he was D.B. Cooper, but the FBI ruled him out by DNA.

segments.title: Kenny Christiansen and L.D. Cooper suspects
segments.summary: Kenny Christiansen, a former Northwest Orient purser and paratrooper, was outed by his brother Lyle. Christiansen's niece says her uncle L.D. came home bruised at Thanksgiving 1971 and claimed a hijacking had solved money problems.

segments.title: Legacy, D.B. Cooper Days, and Larry Carr
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the D.B. Cooper Days festival in Ariel, Drop Zone forum posts, FBI agent Larry Carr's YouTube release of evidence, the DNA on the tie, and the changes in airline security. They close with the Cooper vane on the 727 aft staircase.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts sign off the live show, followed by a closing note directing listeners to HowStuffWorks.com.
